data.source_title: Improving Emergency Department radiology transportation time: a successful implementation of lean methodology
data.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study setting and population and revised process; Results
data.source_setting: American University of Beirut Medical Center academic urban ED; approximately 49,000 annual visits; on-site ED radiography room
data.source_period: Six months pre versus six months post, separated by one-month washout
data.source_n: 6,186 radiographs pre-intervention and 4,879 post-intervention; all ED plain-film patients during six-month comparison periods
data.quantity: Observed mean order-to-transport-completion time for plain radiography
data.source_evidence_basis: Original full-text XML: order-processing-to-study-completion mean TAT fell from 22.89±22.05 to 9.87±15.05 min (p<0.0001); 71.6% versus 32.3% completed within 10 min. Cohort sizes were 6,186 pre and 4,879 post radiographs. Changes included a pending-request dashboard and peak-hours dedicated transporter; preliminary resident reads and final attending reads were separate.
data.limitations: Plain radiography in one ED with an on-site suite; intervention included a dedicated transporter during peak hours. Not CT/MRI scheduling. Mean, SD and threshold share do not fully specify a distribution.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent transport request queue and transporter availability separately from imaging-room capacity; account for local modality, acuity, preparation, and staffing before applying any timing. Include preliminary and final reporting as distinct events.
data.retrieval_timestamp_precision: day; time not logged during source inspection, midnight is a date placeholder
